visible_text: A circle has diameter AB = 12 cm, so its radius is 6 cm. Chord CD of the circle has length 6 cm. The shaded region is bounded by the diameter AB, arc AD, chord DC, and arc CB. Find the area of the shaded region. (A) (12π – 9) cm², (B) (12π + 9) cm², (C) (12π – 9√3) cm², (D) (12π + 9√3) cm².
reasoning: The shaded region is the semicircle minus the circular segment formed by chord CD. The semicircle area is ½π(6)² = 18π. Triangle OCD is equilateral, giving central angle 60°. The sector area is (60°/360°)·π·6² = 6π, the triangle area is (√3/4)·6² = 9√3, so the segment area is 6π – 9√3. Subtracting from the semicircle gives 18π – (6π – 9√3) = 12π + 9√3 cm², which corresponds to option D.
